summary: The enterprise AI model API aggregator landscape in 2026 is dominated by the three major hyperscalers — AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI/Foundry, and Google Vertex AI — each offering multiple foundation models behind a managed API that keeps data within the customer's cloud security perimeter. Data-platform-native options like Snowflake Cortex (product revenue up 26% YoY to $996.8M in Q1 FY2026) and Databricks are gaining fast traction by bringing models to where governed enterprise data already lives, while IBM watsonx, Oracle Cloud AI, and Cloudflare Workers AI serve more specialized niches. There is no single winner — the best fit is largely determined by an organization's existing cloud footprint, governance maturity, and compliance requirements.
why_enterprises_use_aggregators: Data residency and security: models are called within the company's own cloud/VPC perimeter so proprietary data and prompts never leave the governed environment or train vendor models.

Consolidated billing and existing cloud contracts: usage flows through established enterprise agreements (EDPs, committed spend, marketplace credits) rather than separate vendor invoices and new procurement cycles.

Compliance and governance: built-in audit logging, SOC 2/HIPAA/FedRAMP/ISO certifications, IAM-based access control, and data-processing agreements satisfy regulated-industry requirements out of the box.

Model choice and portability: a single API abstracts multiple providers (Claude, Llama, Mistral, Gemini, GPT, Cohere, Nova), avoiding lock-in to one model vendor and allowing swaps as price/performance shifts.
Integrated enterprise tooling: native RAG/knowledge bases, vector search, agent orchestration, fine-tuning, and observability reduce the glue code needed versus stitching together raw vendor APIs.

platforms.name: Azure OpenAI Service / Azure AI Foundry
available_models: select open-weight and partner models via Foundry Model Catalog
platforms.pricing: Pay-as-you-go per 1K/1M tokens plus Provisioned Throughput Units (PTUs) for reserved capacity; billed through Azure enterprise agreement.
platforms.best_for: Microsoft-first enterprises already standardized on Azure, M365, and Entra ID that want first-party OpenAI models.

platforms.name: AWS Bedrock
platforms.pricing: On-demand per-token pricing plus Provisioned Throughput for reserved capacity; billed through AWS account and EDP commitments.
platforms.best_for: AWS-native enterprises with IAM as the identity source of truth that want the widest multi-provider model choice behind one API.

platforms.name: Google Vertex AI Model Garden
platforms.pricing: Pay-as-you-go per token/character plus GSU (Generative AI Scale Unit) reserved throughput — e.g. 25 GSUs of Gemini 2.5 Flash yields ~67,250 tokens/sec sustained; billed via GCP.
platforms.best_for: GCP-heavy organizations and data/ML teams wanting Gemini plus a broad Model Garden and strong MLOps tooling.

platforms.name: Snowflake Cortex AI
platforms.pricing: Consumption-based, billed in Snowflake credits as part of product revenue; no separate model infrastructure to manage.
platforms.best_for: Enterprises with data already governed in Snowflake wanting AI/RAG/agents to run where the data lives without moving it.

platforms.name: Databricks (Mosaic AI / Model Serving)
platforms.pricing: Consumption-based DBUs for model serving and training; billed through Databricks/cloud marketplace.
platforms.best_for: Data engineering and ML teams on the lakehouse that need to fine-tune, serve, and govern custom and open models alongside their data.

platforms.name: IBM watsonx
platforms.pricing: Subscription and consumption tiers (Resource Units); commercial structure requires governance scrutiny per enterprise relationships.
platforms.best_for: Regulated enterprises with significant existing IBM relationships that prioritize AI governance, hybrid/on-prem deployment, and model risk management.

platforms.name: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) Generative AI
platforms.pricing: Pay-as-you-go per-character/token plus dedicated AI cluster hosting for reserved capacity; billed via OCI and Universal Credits.
platforms.best_for: Oracle database and ERP/Fusion application customers wanting GenAI embedded near their Oracle data estate.

platforms.name: Cloudflare Workers AI
available_models: models accessible via AI Gateway to OpenAI/Anthropic
platforms.pricing: Usage-based (neurons/tokens) with generous free tier; pay-as-you-go on the Cloudflare developer platform.
platforms.best_for: Developers and enterprises needing low-latency, globally distributed edge inference and a unified gateway in front of multiple model vendors.
